steps: Before each consultation, print the question sheet or open the Consult Questions tab.
After each meeting, enter the lawyer's rate, estimated hours, flat fee or percentage in the yellow cells.
Read each draft fee agreement with the 23-point check. Ask about every No or Unclear.
Compare the estimated totals and watch-outs, not the hourly rates.
After hiring, log invoices in the Bill Tracker; it flags rate mismatches and budget overruns.
forWho: Anyone collecting quotes from two or three lawyers
People about to sign a retainer or contingency agreement
Small business owners hiring a lawyer for a defined project
Clients who want to check invoices against the agreement
notFor: People looking for legal advice on their case: talk to a lawyer
People who qualify for free legal aid (see our legal aid guide)
Anyone wanting a prediction of what a case is worth
compat: Excel 365, LibreOffice Calc 7+ and Google Sheets (File → Import; sheet protection is not carried over). PDFs are US Letter and fillable in Adobe Acrobat Reader and most browser PDF viewers.
limits: It does not tell you which lawyer to hire or whether a fee is "fair"; it puts quotes on the same basis so you can ask better questions.
Totals are only as good as the estimates the lawyers give you.
It is not legal advice and does not review your agreement for legal validity.

faq.q: Can I compare a contingency quote with an hourly quote?
faq.a: Yes. Enter an amount you assume might be recovered; the toolkit shows the contingency fee and what you would receive, next to the hourly and flat-fee totals. We do not estimate what your case is worth.
